title: Bhagavad Gita
author: vyasa
attributionNote: Traditionally attributed to Vyasa and embedded in the Mahabharata. Modern scholarship treats the Gita as a composite philosophical poem shaped within the epic tradition.
description: Set on the eve of battle, the Gita records Krishna's instruction to Arjuna on duty, action, knowledge and devotion. The complete eighteen chapters are read here in Edwin Arnold's 1885 verse translation, from the opening distress of Arjuna to the final account of renunciation.
historicalContext: The Gita synthesises strands of Brahmanical, Samkhya, Yoga and devotional thought. It has been interpreted by competing schools and has become one of the most widely translated Hindu texts. Arnold's The Song Celestial was one of the first English verse translations to reach a general readership.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1885 translation by Edwin Arnold is public domain in the United States.
